newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mostly up on export hopes.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mostly up on export hopes.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled mostly higher after receiving an early boost from commercial-related buying, traders said.
Wheat prices gained early as Wilson Trading bought at least two million March bushels. Traders said the purchase was likely tied to export business.

U.S. wheat also drew support early from a U.S. Wheat Associates analyst's forecast in Washington that India may need to import one million tonnes of wheat over the coming months. Wheat was underpinned by ideas that Russia and Iraq could buy U.S. wheat.
But spring wheat prices were on the defensive late as Atwood-Peavey sold 1.5 million March bushels. Traders speculated this was linked to positioning ahead of Thursday's USDA December crop report.
Overall, MGE spring wheat closed 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower to seven cents higher, with Dec down 5-1/4 cents at $4.16-1/2. March gained 1-3/4 to close at $3.80-3/4.
Apart from Wilson and Atwood-Peavey, players included Country Hedging, which sold 1.7 million March, traders said. Spread activity was heavy, they said.
MGE barley futures did not trade and closed unchanged.
